idiom_name: Vapor Fluent Model (final class + property wrappers) with create/save/delete
implementation_notes: Fluent, the Vapor ORM, models a table as a final class conforming to Model: the static schema names the table, @ID/@Field/@OptionalField/@Timestamp property wrappers declare identity, columns and audit timestamps, and the instance persists itself with create/save/delete (and restore for soft-deleted rows) against a Database, while Planet.query(on: db) is the finder. What replaces the classic structure is Codable reflection plus property wrappers, so the mapping is declared inline and no mapper object exists; GRDB's PersistableRecord (save/insert/update on the record type) is the same shape for plain SQLite. Use it when the service already speaks Fluent; otherwise Core Data's NSManagedObjectContext is a different, unit-of-work-shaped model.
pitfalls: Models are reference types without an identity map: two instances of the same row can hold divergent state, and the last save wins unless the column set is narrowed.
@ID is optional until the row is stored (requireID to unwrap), and the class needs an empty initialiser plus the wrappers - a plain struct cannot be a Fluent model.
Models are not Sendable across concurrency domains, so background work should pass identifiers or values rather than the model instance itself.
